label.ta: Exercise 8.2 · Q1 (English only; Tamil review pending)

title.en: Coefficient of variation from standard deviation and mean

q.en: 1. The standard deviation and mean of a data are 6.5 and 12.5 respectively. Find the coefficient of variation.

steps.en: Write what is given. Symbols: σ (sigma) is the standard deviation, which measures how spread out the data are; x̄ (x-bar) is the mean, the average value; C.V. is the coefficient of variation, which writes the spread as a percentage of the mean so that different data sets can be compared. Formula: C.V. = σ/x̄ × 100%.
Substitute the two values into the formula.
Clear the decimals by multiplying the top and bottom by 2: 6.5 × 2 = 13 and 12.5 × 2 = 25.
Multiply by 100. Since 100 ÷ 25 = 4, the fraction becomes 13 × 4.
Check by reversing: 52 % of the mean should be the standard deviation: 0.52 × 12.5 = 6.5.

label.ta: Exercise 8.2 · Q2 (English only; Tamil review pending)

title.en: Mean from standard deviation and coefficient of variation

q.en: 2. The standard deviation and coefficient of variation of a data are 1.2 and 25.6 respectively. Find the value of mean.

steps.en: Write what is given. Symbols: σ (sigma) is the standard deviation, which measures how spread out the data are; x̄ (x-bar) is the mean, the average value; C.V. is the coefficient of variation, which writes the spread as a percentage of the mean so that different data sets can be compared. Formula: C.V. = σ/x̄ × 100%. Here the mean x̄ is unknown.
Multiply both sides by x̄ and divide both sides by 25.6 to get x̄ alone.
Simplify: 1.2 × 100 = 120. Multiply top and bottom by 10 to remove the decimal, then divide both by 16.

title.en: Standard deviation from mean and coefficient of variation

q.en: 3. If the mean and coefficient of variation of a data are 15 and 48 respectively, then find the value of standard deviation.

steps.en: Write what is given. Symbols: σ (sigma) is the standard deviation, which measures how spread out the data are; x̄ (x-bar) is the mean, the average value; C.V. is the coefficient of variation, which writes the spread as a percentage of the mean so that different data sets can be compared. Formula: C.V. = σ/x̄ × 100%. Here the standard deviation σ is unknown.
Multiply both sides by 15 and divide both sides by 100 to get σ alone.
